mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by statistically significant negative returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth for cyclicals and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or not statistically different from baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index below 2% for two months signals a monetary policy shift toward disinflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances or not statistically lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a precautionary savings cycle, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases and GDPC1 decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate cost pressures, ultimately supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates fall.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
